title: At a Restaurant
pronunciation_focus_summary: The French R (uvular fricative) — found in restaurant, garçon, addition, and dozens of essential dining words. Made in the back of the throat, not with the tongue tip.

phrases.translation: I would like to reserve a table
phrases.pronunciation_notes: Three French R sounds in this phrase. Practice the uvular R — soft gargle in the back of the throat.
phrases.example_sentence: Je voudrais réserver une table pour ce soir.

phrases.text: Une table pour deux, s'il vous plaît
phrases.phonetic_ipa: yn tabl puʁ dø sil vu plɛ
phrases.phonetic_approx: oon TAHBL poor DUH seel voo PLEH
phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'pour' has the French R. 'Deux' has the 'eu' sound — round lips and say 'uh'.
phrases.example_sentence: Bonsoir, une table pour deux, s'il vous plaît.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The French R in 'carte' is followed by a 't' — practice the R-T transition.
phrases.example_sentence: Est-ce que je peux avoir la carte, s'il vous plaît ?

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The R in 'recommandez' starts the stressed part. The nasal 'an' appears in the middle.
phrases.example_sentence: Qu'est-ce que vous recommandez comme plat du jour ?

phrases.text: Je prends le plat du jour
phrases.phonetic_ipa: ʒə pʁɑ̃ lə pla dy ʒuʁ
phrases.phonetic_approx: zhuh PRAHN luh PLAH doo ZHOOR
phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'ds' in 'prends' is silent. The nasal 'an' sound. 'Jour' ends with the French R.
phrases.example_sentence: Je prends le plat du jour et une carafe d'eau.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'en' is a nasal vowel. The 'ée' at the end is a clear 'ay' sound. French R in the middle.
phrases.example_sentence: Comme entrée, je voudrais la soupe à l'oignon.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'in' in 'principal' is a nasal vowel. Silent 't' in 'plat'. The French R appears once.
phrases.example_sentence: Le plat principal est excellent ici.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The final 't' is silent. The French R ends the word. Both 'e' sounds are open.
phrases.example_sentence: Comme dessert, qu'est-ce que vous avez ?

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'ien' at the end is a nasal vowel. Multiple French R sounds. The 'é' is closed E.
phrases.example_sentence: Je suis végétarien, est-ce qu'il y a des options sans viande ?

phrases.pronunciation_notes: Ordering 'une carafe d'eau' gets you free tap water. The 'af' in 'carafe' — the 'f' IS pronounced.
phrases.example_sentence: Une carafe d'eau pour la table, s'il vous plaît.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: Two nasal vowels: 'in' and 'an'. 'Blanc' — the 'c' is silent. The 'bl' cluster is smooth.
phrases.example_sentence: Du vin blanc de Bourgogne, s'il vous plaît.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'on' in 'bon' is a nasal vowel. The 'è' in 'très' is an open E. French R in 'très'.
phrases.example_sentence: C'est très bon ! Mes compliments au chef.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: The 'tion' ending is 'syohn' with a nasal vowel — not 'shun' like English.
phrases.example_sentence: Quand vous aurez un moment, l'addition s'il vous plaît.

phrases.pronunciation_notes: Liaison: 'suis‿allergique'. Two French R sounds. The 'g' before 'i' is soft ('zh').
Liaison: 'bon‿appétit' — the 'n' links to the 'a'. The final 't' is actually pronounced here (exception!).

exchanges.speaker: waiter
exchanges.translation: Good evening! Do you have a reservation?

exchanges.speaker: you
exchanges.text: Oui, au nom de Martin. Une table pour deux.
exchanges.translation: Yes, under the name Martin. A table for two.
exchanges.phonetic_approx: WEE, oh NOHN duh mahr-TAHN. oon TAHBL poor DUH

exchanges.speaker: waiter
exchanges.text: Très bien. Suivez-moi. Voici la carte.
exchanges.translation: Very well. Follow me. Here's the menu.
exchanges.phonetic_approx: treh BYEHN. swee-VAY mwah. vwah-SEE lah KAHRT

exchanges.speaker: you
exchanges.translation: Thank you. What do you recommend?

dialogues.notes: Making reservations is common for dinner in France. Lunch is often more casual. Say 'Bonsoir' (not 'Bonjour') for evening dining.

dialogues.context: Discussing dietary needs with the waiter

exchanges.speaker: you
exchanges.text: Excusez-moi, je suis végétarien. Qu'est-ce que vous proposez ?
exchanges.translation: Excuse me, I'm vegetarian. What do you suggest?
exchanges.phonetic_approx: ex-koo-ZAY mwah, zhuh SWEE vay-zhay-tah-RYEHN. kess kuh voo proh-poh-ZAY?

exchanges.speaker: waiter
exchanges.text: Bien sûr. Nous avons une salade niçoise et un risotto aux légumes.
exchanges.translation: Of course. We have a niçoise salad and a vegetable risotto.
exchanges.phonetic_approx: byehn SOOR. nooz ah-VOHN oon sah-LAHD nee-SWAHZ ay uhn ree-ZOH-toh oh lay-GOOM

exchanges.speaker: you
exchanges.text: Le risotto, s'il vous plaît. Et une carafe d'eau.
exchanges.translation: The risotto, please. And a carafe of water.
exchanges.phonetic_approx: luh ree-ZOH-toh seel voo PLEH. ay oon kah-RAHF DOH

dialogues.notes: Vegetarian options are increasingly common in French restaurants. 'Sans viande' (without meat) and 'sans poisson' (without fish) are useful phrases.

cultural_notes.title: French dining etiquette
cultural_notes.content: French dining is a social ritual. Meals are structured: apéritif (pre-dinner drink), entrée (starter), plat principal (main), fromage (cheese), dessert. Lunch break is sacred — typically 12-2pm. Dinner starts later, around 7:30-8pm. Bread is placed directly on the table, not on a plate. Hands should stay above the table (not in your lap). Service is included in the price ('service compris'), so tipping is optional but rounding up is appreciated.
